hints.title: Tree Centroid Convergence Obstacle
hints.text: A tree has at most two centroids that minimize root-to-leaf path length. Finding them by testing every node is inefficient. How can trimming boundary extremities layer by layer converge to the geometric center?

hints.title: Centroid Degree-One Trimming Invariant
hints.text: Centroids lie at the midpoint of the longest tree diameter. Removing all current nodes with degree one preserves the central nodes until at most two remain.

hints.title: Leaf Elimination Inward Pruning Procedure
hints.text: If n <= 2, return all nodes directly. Build an adjacency structure and locate all nodes with degree 1. Repeatedly peel off degree 1 nodes layer by layer, updating degrees and isolating new degree 1 nodes until two or fewer nodes remain. Return those remaining nodes.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Each vertex and edge is removed at most once during leaf trimming.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Running path calculations from every vertex takes O(V^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Adjacency sets and leaves buffers consume linear space O(V).
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing that any tree has either 1 or 2 centroids and trimming leaves inwards.
